---
title: "05 — Closed-loop suspension (loop-bias, cancelled)"
---

The most realistic case: a suspension identified **with its damping loop closed**.
The feedback fights the very resonance we are trying to measure, so the instrument
no longer shows the open-loop plant `P`. It shows the *closed-loop* response

$$
T = \frac{P}{1 + PC},
$$

whose resonant peak is suppressed by the loop gain $1 + PC$. Fitting `T` and calling
it the plant is **biased** — a loop-ignorant fit understates the plant gain near the
resonance.

The classic fix is to measure `T`, then divide the controller back out,
$\hat{P} = \hat{T}/(1 - \hat{T}C)$. That needs the controller `C` as a known object
and a fragile hand-division *after* the fit — and an earlier version of this example
listed a "controller-aware estimator" as future work.

**That future work now exists.** With the loop genuinely closed in the digital twin,
the Pintelon–Schoukens **reference-based FRF** — the ratio of period-averaged spectra
$\overline{Y}/\overline{X}$ read off the drive monitor and the response — cancels the
controller automatically and returns the **open-loop plant directly**. No controller
object, no division. We inject a periodic multisine, measure the leakage-free FRF, and
fit it by maximum likelihood with `GMLEstimator`. We still use `python-control`, but
only to *draw* the suppressed closed-loop `T` for the bias story — never in the fit.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
import control as ct

from system_ident.backends.twin import TwinBackend
from system_ident.plant import SuspensionPlant
from system_ident.model import TFModel
from system_ident.excitation import multisine_from_psd
from system_ident.loop import SysIDLoop
from system_ident.estimators.gml import GMLEstimator

FS, NPERSEG, N_PERIODS = 32.0, 2048, 8
TOTAL = NPERSEG * N_PERIODS / FS

# True open-loop plant: a single 1 Hz, Q = 20 suspension resonance.
P_TRUE = TFModel.from_resonances([(1.0, 20.0)], 100.0)
plant = SuspensionPlant({"POS": P_TRUE}, FS)

# Velocity-damping controller C(s) = k s / (1 + s/wc), proper, negative feedback.
k, wc = 2e-3, 2 * np.pi * 12.0
C = ([k, 0.0], [1.0 / wc, 1.0])

# Close the loop *inside* the twin by passing controllers=.
tw = TwinBackend(
    plant, {"C1:EXC": "POS"}, {"C1:RSP": "POS"}, fs=FS,
    sensor_asd=1e-4, disturbance_asd=1e-4, controllers={"POS": C}, seed=3,
)

# Synchronous excitation grid: every line lands exactly on a DFT bin.
f_all = np.fft.rfftfreq(NPERSEG, 1 / FS)
band = (f_all >= 0.1) & (f_all <= 5.0)
freq = f_all[band]
Pxx = np.ones_like(freq)            # flat in-band budget (the FRF is scale-free)
```

## Measure through the closed loop — and recover the open-loop plant

We inject the periodic multisine as the loop *reference*, then read the **drive
monitor** (`C1:EXC`, the actuator signal the loop actually sends) and the
**response** (`C1:RSP`). The reference-based ratio-of-averages
$\overline{Y}/\overline{X}$ projects onto the deterministic multisine, which is
uncorrelated with the fed-back loop and sensor noise; that projection **cancels the
controller** and the returned `H` is the *open-loop* plant — with **no** manual
$1/(1 - TC)$ step anywhere.

```{python}
tw.inject("C1:EXC", multisine_from_psd(Pxx, FS, NPERSEG, N_PERIODS, freq, seed=0), FS)
seg = tw.read(["C1:EXC", "C1:RSP"], TOTAL)

# THIS H is already the OPEN-LOOP plant — the loop is cancelled by the ratio.
H, H_err, _ = SysIDLoop._estimate_tf_periodic(seg["C1:EXC"], seg["C1:RSP"], FS, NPERSEG, band)
exc = np.isfinite(H_err)

prior = TFModel.from_resonances([(1.3, 14.0)], 130.0)   # ~30% off in f0 and Q
P_hat = GMLEstimator().fit(freq, H, H_err, prior)


def _f0_q(model):
    p = np.roots(np.asarray(model.den, float))
    p = p[p.imag > 1e-9][0]
    w0 = abs(p)
    return w0 / (2 * np.pi), w0 / (2 * abs(p.real))


f0t, qt = _f0_q(P_TRUE)
f0h, qh = _f0_q(P_hat)
print(f"true open-loop  : f0 = {f0t:.3f} Hz, Q = {qt:.1f}")
print(f"recovered P_hat : f0 = {f0h:.3f} Hz, Q = {qh:.1f}   (no controller-division)")
```

## Is the drive gentle? — the measurement time series

Even with the loop closed, the reference is a periodic Schroeder multisine: a smooth,
bounded, low-crest waveform, not an impulsive kick. The drive monitor (the signal the
controller actually pushes) stays well inside a safe actuator range, and the response
is a steady bounded oscillation — partly knocked down by the feedback.

```{python}
#| label: fig-closedloop-timeseries
#| fig-cap: "First ~64 s of the closed-loop measurement. The drive monitor (top) is a smooth low-crest multisine; the response (bottom) is a bounded oscillation, partly suppressed by the damping loop. Peak drive stays well inside a safe actuator range."

SKY, GOLD, RED, GRAY = '#1F8AC0', '#C8973A', '#E53E3E', '#94A3B8'
t = np.arange(int(64 * FS)) / FS
fig = make_subplots(
    rows=2, cols=1, shared_xaxes=True, vertical_spacing=0.09,
    subplot_titles=['<b>Drive monitor</b> — actuator signal (Schroeder multisine, loop closed)',
                    '<b>Response</b> — suspension motion (damped by the loop)'],
)
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=t, y=seg['C1:EXC'][:t.size], mode='lines',
              line=dict(color=SKY, width=1.3), name='drive monitor'), row=1, col=1)
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=t, y=seg['C1:RSP'][:t.size], mode='lines',
              line=dict(color=GOLD, width=1.5), name='response'), row=2, col=1)
fig.update_layout(template='plotly_white', height=460,
                  margin=dict(l=60, r=20, t=50, b=50),
                  font=dict(family='Outfit, Inter, sans-serif', size=12),
                  legend=dict(orientation='h', yanchor='bottom', y=1.05, xanchor='right', x=1))
fig.update_yaxes(title_text='drive [cts]', row=1, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig.update_yaxes(title_text='motion [a.u.]', row=2, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig.update_xaxes(title_text='time [s]', row=2, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig.show()
```

## The bias story — and its cancellation

For the picture only, we use `python-control` to form the closed-loop response
$T = \text{feedback}(P, C)$ that the instrument *would* report if you fit the raw
closed-loop transfer function. Its resonant peak is visibly suppressed — that is the
bias. The recovered $\hat{P}$, by contrast, lands right on the true open-loop plant.

```{python}
def to_tfmodel(sys):
    """Convert a python-control TransferFunction to TFModel (for plotting |T| only)."""
    sys = ct.tf(sys)
    num = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(sys.num[0][0], dtype=float))
    den = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(sys.den[0][0], dtype=float))
    return TFModel(num=num, den=den)

P_ct = ct.tf(list(P_TRUE.num), list(P_TRUE.den))
C_ct = ct.tf(*C)
T_model = to_tfmodel(ct.minreal(ct.feedback(P_ct, C_ct)))   # closed-loop, suppressed
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-closedloop
#| fig-cap: "The closed loop suppresses the resonance in T (grey dotted), so fitting T is biased. The Pintelon–Schoukens reference-based FRF (grey points) sits on the true open-loop plant P (blue) with the loop closed, and the ML fit P̂ (gold dashed) recovers it — with no controller-division. Zoom near 1 Hz; toggle traces in the legend."

fgrid = np.logspace(np.log10(0.1), np.log10(5.0), 600)

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=fgrid, y=np.abs(P_TRUE.eval(fgrid)), mode='lines',
    line=dict(color=SKY, width=2.8), name='True open-loop plant P',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   |P| = %{y:.4g}<extra></extra>'))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=fgrid, y=np.abs(T_model.eval(fgrid)), mode='lines',
    line=dict(color=GRAY, width=1.8, dash='dot'),
    name='Closed-loop T  (biased — feedback suppresses resonance)',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   |T| = %{y:.4g}<extra></extra>'))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq[exc], y=np.abs(H[exc]), mode='markers',
    marker=dict(color='rgba(148,163,184,0.6)', size=4),
    name='Reference-based FRF  (open-loop, loop closed)',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   |H| = %{y:.4g}<extra></extra>'))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=fgrid, y=np.abs(P_hat.eval(fgrid)), mode='lines',
    line=dict(color=GOLD, width=2.2, dash='dash'),
    name='Recovered P̂  (ML fit, no controller-division)',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   |P̂| = %{y:.4g}<extra></extra>'))

idx_res = int(np.argmax(np.abs(P_TRUE.eval(fgrid))))
fig.add_annotation(
    x=np.log10(fgrid[idx_res]), y=np.log10(np.abs(T_model.eval(fgrid))[idx_res]),
    text='<b>Resonance<br>suppressed in T</b>',
    showarrow=True, arrowhead=2, arrowsize=1.1, arrowcolor='rgba(148,163,184,0.7)',
    ax=-80, ay=30, font=dict(size=10, color=GRAY, family='Outfit, sans-serif'))

fig.update_layout(
    template='plotly_white', height=440,
    margin=dict(l=60, r=20, t=20, b=55),
    font=dict(family='Outfit, Inter, sans-serif', size=12),
    legend=dict(orientation='h', yanchor='bottom', y=1.02, xanchor='right', x=1,
                bgcolor='rgba(255,255,255,0.9)', bordercolor='#DCE5F0', borderwidth=1,
                font=dict(size=10)),
    xaxis=dict(title='Frequency  [Hz]', type='log', gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)'),
    yaxis=dict(title='|G(f)|', type='log', gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)'))
fig.show()
```

::: {.callout-important}
## The bias is real — and it is cancelled, not corrected

Near the 1 Hz resonance the damping loop suppresses the closed-loop peak by the loop
gain $1 + PC$: a loop-ignorant fit of `T` reports a softened, understated resonance.
The old remedy measured `T` and *divided* the controller back out by hand. Here the
reference-based ratio-of-averages **cancels the loop in the measurement itself** — the
grey FRF points already lie on the open-loop plant, so `P̂` is unbiased without ever
naming `C` in the fit. At LIGO, where control gain can be 40 dB or more near a pendulum
resonance, cancelling the loop at the measurement is far more robust than a post-hoc
division.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Controller-aware identification is now built in

There is nothing left as "future work" here: closing the loop in the twin and reading
the reference-based FRF *is* the controller-aware estimator. The same code path a real
closed-loop measurement uses — inject a periodic multisine, read the drive monitor and
response, average the spectra over periods — returns the open-loop plant directly.
:::
